turns.question: Under Rule 14a-8 in Title 17, what ownership and holding-period requirements must a shareholder meet to have a proposal included in a company's proxy statement? Cite the section.

report.markdown:
Under **17 CFR § 240.14a-8(b)(1)(i)**, a shareholder must meet one of three tiered ownership-and-holding-period thresholds, based on the **market value** of the company's voting securities they have **continuously held**:

| Minimum Market Value | Minimum Continuous Holding Period |
|----------------------|-----------------------------------|
| **$2,000** | **3 years** |
| **$15,000** | **2 years** |
| **$25,000** | **1 year** |

The securities must be “entitled to vote on the proposal.” The shareholder must also provide a written statement of intent to continue holding the required amount through the date of the shareholders’ meeting [1].

hits.snippet: § 240.14a-8 Shareholder proposals. This section addresses when a company must include a shareholder's proposal in its proxy statement and identify the proposal in its form of proxy when the company holds an annual or special meeting of shareholders. In summary, in order to have your shareholder proposal included on a company's proxy card, and included along with any supporting statement in its proxy statement, you must be eligible and follow certain procedures. Under a few specific circumstances, the company is permitted to exclude your proposal, but only after submitting its reasons to the Commission. We structured this section in a question-and-answer format so that it is easier to understand. The references to “you” are to a shareholder seeking to submit the proposal. (a) Question 1: What is a proposal? A shareholder proposal is your recommendation or requirement that the company and/or its board of directors take action, which you intend to present at a meeting of the company's shareholders. Your proposal should state as clearly as possible the course of action that you believe the company should follow. If your proposal is placed on the company's proxy card, the company must also provide in the form of proxy means for shareholders to specify by boxes a choice between approval or disapproval, or abstention. Unless otherwise indicated, the word “proposal” as used in this section refers both to your proposal, and to your corresponding statement in support of your proposal (
